title: Why Dropbox is a obvious PE Target — S-1
excerpt: I have been doing research on companies, reading 10-Ks, etc.
content_html:
I have been doing research on companies, reading 10-Ks, etc.

I have been doing research on companies, reading 10-Ks, etc. Coming across Dropbox, I felt conflicted. Drew Houston is a great founder, and the Dropbox story is one of many lessons, including an 800 million dollar acquisition offer from Steve Jobs. ICloud went on to become a bigger business than Dropbox. And Sequoia’s investment in Dropbox was a great one, second to Airbnb in Fund 12.

But as of late, reading the 10-K and seeing the slowing growth, there was not much to be optimistic about. Again, Steve Jobs was right: Dropbox was indeed a feature, not a Product, and clearly the wave of enterprise companies that were features that IPOed and struggled is many. Thus, I have a thesis of a wave of consolidation in this sector. And SaaS generally has had a history of strategic consolidation.

Dropbox would not be a strategic acquisition since most of the major enterprise companies already have a solid storage business. But it does throw off cash, and a lot of it. In FY2025, it threw off 931 million in free cash flow. From a Hamilton Hemler perspective, their main power is to allow for sustainable long-term cash flow, which would be switching costs. Once a smb embedes their documents with Dropbox and uses it to manage all their work documents, it creates a switching cost because of the complexities in switching and the harm it could cause in switching; apart from that their is no real other power. The switching costs do allow pricing power, but that is likely fragile.

But while this is no revenue-growing juggernaut, it’s a stable, cash-rich business, which is the kind of ideal target for the likes of a Silver Lake to acquire. And the valuation is cheap, making the debt load ratio reasonable, and use the close to one billion to pay down the debt. You could also take an aggressive approach in reducing headcount and cutting R&D. The product has largely remained the same, and there has not been much innovation since the founding. In terms of an exit strategy, there will probably not be a re-IPO, and finding another acquirer is also improbable. So likely just harvesting cash is the ideal play.

So now here are some rough numbers. As of the time of writing, the Enterprise Value is 6.43 billion. Assuming a 25% premium, the price would be around 8 billion. The FCF growth has been strong, around a 10% 3-year average, and 7% in 2025. Assuming a forward 5-year 3% growth rate. Assuming 60% debt, 4.8 billion, and the rest in sponsor equity.

Overall consolidation is cyclical, and there are periods of IPO booms and many new companies, and then bear markets where the Berkshires of the world buy great assets at even better prices. But a lesson from this story is twofold: when Steve Jobs tries to buy you, take it. Economically, the return from a capital efficiency standpoint would be much better. Second, public companies that are truly just a feature never give you great returns.

content_html_zh:
我一直在做公司研究、阅读10-Ks等。

我一直在做公司研究，阅读10-Ks等。接触Dropbox，我感到很矛盾。 德鲁·休斯顿 (Drew Houston) 是一位伟大的创始人，Dropbox 的故事就是众多教训之一，其中包括史蒂夫·乔布斯 (Steve Jobs) 提出的 8 亿美元收购要约。 ICloud 随后成为比 Dropbox 更大的业务。 红杉资本对 Dropbox 的投资是一笔伟大的投资，在 12 号基金中仅次于 Airbnb。

但截至最近，从 10-K 数据来看，增长放缓，并没有太多值得乐观的地方。 再次强调，史蒂夫·乔布斯是对的：Dropbox 确实是一个功能，而不是一个产品，显然，因功能而上市并陷入困境的企业公司有很多。 因此，我有一个关于该行业整合浪潮的论文。 SaaS 总体上有过战略整合的历史。

Dropbox 不会是一项战略收购，因为大多数大型企业公司已经拥有稳固的存储业务。 但它确实浪费了现金，而且是大量现金。 2025 财年，该公司自由现金流达 9.31 亿美元。 从汉密尔顿·赫姆勒的角度来看，他们的主要力量是允许可持续的长期现金流，这将是转换成本。 一旦中小型企业将其文档嵌入 Dropbox 并使用它来管理所有工作文档，就会产生切换成本，因为切换的复杂性以及切换可能造成的危害；除此之外，他们没有其他真正的力量。 转换成本确实允许定价能力，但这可能很脆弱。

尽管这并不是收入增长的巨头，但它是一项稳定、现金充裕的业务，是银湖等公司收购的理想目标。 而且估值便宜，使得负债率合理，用接近十亿还清债务。 您还可以采取积极的方法来减少员工人数和削减研发费用。 自成立以来，产品基本保持不变，没有太多创新。 从退出策略来看，很可能不会进行重新IPO，寻找另一个收购者也不太可能。 因此，仅仅收获现金可能就是理想的玩法。

现在这里有一些粗略的数字。 截至撰写本文时，企业价值为 64.3 亿。 假设溢价25%，价格在80亿左右。 FCF 增长强劲，三年平均增长约 10%，2025 年将增长 7%。 假设未来 5 年增长率为 3%。 假设 60% 的债务为 48 亿美元，其余为赞助商股权。

整体整合是周期性的，有IPO繁荣时期和许多新公司，然后是熊市，世界各地的伯克希尔公司以更好的价格购买优质资产。 但这个故事的教训是双重的：当史蒂夫·乔布斯试图收购你时，接受它。 从经济角度来看，从资本效率的角度来看，回报会好得多。 其次，真正只是一个功能的上市公司永远不会给你带来丰厚的回报。
